q: Which UK Act forms the legal foundation for all workplace health and safety law?

options.C: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974
options.D: Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999

answer: C — Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974.

q: An HSE ______ Notice stops a dangerous activity immediately.
answer: Prohibition.

q: Name one legal duty a worker holds under Section 7 of the Health and Safety at Work Act.
answer: To take reasonable care of their own health and safety and that of others affected by their actions (or to cooperate with their employer on safety matters).

q: A Principal Contractor is only required under CDM 2015 when more than one contractor is involved on a project.
answer: True.

q: Which of the following must happen before a worker starts work on a new site?
answer: D — Site induction.

q: Appealing a Prohibition Notice does ______ suspend its effect.
answer: Not.

q: Under Section 37 of the Health and Safety at Work Act, who besides the company can be personally prosecuted for a serious breach?
answer: Individual directors or managers.

q: What is the first step in the hierarchy of control measures?
answer: C — Eliminate the hazard.

q: A risk assessment must be reviewed whenever site ______ change.
answer: Conditions.

q: What is the difference between a hazard and a risk?
answer: A hazard is anything with the potential to cause harm; a risk is the likelihood of that harm happening, combined with how severe it would be.

q: A method statement can be reused without changes for a similar task on a different site.
answer: False — it must be specific to the actual task and site conditions.

q: Which HSE step comes immediately after "identify the hazards"?

options.A: Decide who might be harmed and how

answer: A — Decide who might be harmed and how.

q: PPE is considered the ______ resort in the hierarchy of control.
answer: Last.

q: What should a worker do if they spot a new hazard partway through a task that wasn't in the original risk assessment?
answer: Report it immediately, so the risk assessment can be reviewed and updated before work continues.

q: Under RIDDOR, how soon must a death at work be reported to HSE?
answer: D — Without delay.

q: An over-7-day injury must be reported within ______ days of the accident.
What is a near miss, and why should it still be reported even though no one was harmed?
answer: A near miss is an event where no one was harmed but easily could have been; it should be reported because it reveals the same gap in control an accident would, before someone is actually hurt.

q: A dry powder extinguisher is safe to use on an electrical fire above 1000 volts.
answer: False — dry powder is only safe on electrical fires up to 1000V, not above it.

q: Which colour label identifies a CO2 extinguisher?
answer: B — Black.

q: The three elements of the fire triangle are heat, fuel, and ______.
answer: Oxygen.

q: What is the first thing a worker should do when a fire alarm sounds?
answer: Stop work immediately and proceed via the nearest safe route to the designated assembly point.

q: Which regulations specifically require employers to assess and control exposure to substances hazardous to health? A) COSHH 2002
answer: A — COSHH 2002.

q: The workplace exposure limit for respirable crystalline silica is ______ mg/m³ as an 8-hour time-weighted average.
What should a worker do if they suspect they've uncovered asbestos-containing material?
answer: Stop work immediately, avoid disturbing the material further, and report it so it can be properly identified before work continues.

q: Tight-fitting RPE can still protect a worker effectively even if they have facial hair along the seal line.
answer: False — facial hair along the seal line breaks the seal and compromises protection, regardless of the mask's rating.

q: At what noise level does hearing protection become mandatory under the Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005?
answer: C — 85 dB(A).

q: The exposure limit value for hand-arm vibration is ______ m/s² A(8).
What does the "L" in the TILE manual handling framework stand for, and what does it cover?
answer: Load — the weight, size, shape, and stability of the object being handled, including whether its contents could shift.

q: Under CDM 2015 Schedule 2, which facility may specifically be required because of a hazard such as cement contact?
answer: B — Showers.

q: A worker whose prescription medication affects their ability to work safely has a duty to ______ this to their employer.
answer: Disclose (or report).

q: Why is prolonged skin contact with wet cement a serious hazard, not just a minor irritation?
answer: Wet cement is highly alkaline, and prolonged contact can cause genuine chemical burns, not just dryness or irritation.

q: Mental health is covered by the same general duty of care an employer owes for physical health and safety.
answer: True.

q: What is the correct immediate response if a worker shows confusion or collapses in hot conditions on site?

options.A: Give them a hot drink and continue working
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to report it
options.C: Encourage them to keep moving to stay alert
options.D: Treat it as a medical emergency and seek help immediately

answer: D — Treat it as a medical emergency and seek help immediately.

q: Cement's hazard to skin comes from its high ______, which can cause chemical burns on prolonged contact.
answer: Alkalinity.

q: What should a worker do if they believe a colleague may be unfit for work due to substance use or impairment?
answer: Report it to a supervisor rather than ignoring it, since an impaired colleague is a safety risk to themselves and everyone working around them.

q: Who is responsible for paying for PPE provided to protect against a workplace risk?

options.A: The worker, through a payroll deduction
options.B: Shared equally between the worker and the employer

answer: D — The employer, free of charge.

q: PPE sits at the ______ of the hierarchy of control, used only once other measures cannot remove the risk.
answer: Bottom (last resort).

q: Why might a worker with a beard along the mask seal line need to be refit tested or issued different RPE?
answer: Facial hair along the seal line breaks the mask's seal against the skin, letting contaminated air in, so the worker needs a refit test on a different mask or RPE that doesn't rely on a tight seal, such as a powered respirator.

q: Earmuffs and earplugs should always be worn together for maximum hearing protection.
answer: False — combining them is only used where a risk assessment shows a single type isn't enough; over-protecting by default can isolate a worker from alarms and warnings.

q: What shape is used for a mandatory safety sign, such as one reading 'Wear eye protection'?
answer: A — Circle.

q: A red circle with a diagonal line through a black symbol is a ______ sign.
answer: Prohibition.

q: Why is a safety sign's shape as important as its colour?
answer: Shape lets a colour-blind worker, or one working in poor light, still recognise a sign's meaning from its outline alone, without depending on seeing colour correctly.

q: Under the Work at Height Regulations 2005, what should be considered first when planning a task at height?

options.B: Avoiding the work at height altogether

answer: B — Avoiding the work at height altogether.

q: A leaning ladder should be set so the base sits one unit from the wall for every ______ units of working height (the 1 in 4 rule).
answer: Four.

q: Why does a scaffold need a competent person to inspect it every 7 days, not just once when it's first erected?
answer: Conditions such as weather, ground movement, or site activity can cause a scaffold to deteriorate or be altered after erection, so regular reinspection confirms it's still safe to use, with extra checks after events like storms or substantial alteration.

q: A fall restraint system and a fall arrest system do the same job.
answer: False — restraint physically prevents a worker from reaching a fall hazard at all, while arrest only catches a worker after a fall has already begun, and needs a rescue plan because of the risk of suspension trauma.

q: Which method of preventing a leaning ladder from slipping is used only as a last resort?

options.A: Tying both stiles to a suitable point
options.D: Wedging the base of the ladder

answer: C — Footing the ladder.

q: The top guardrail on a construction working platform must be at least ______ millimetres above the platform.
Why should a worker never step directly onto a fragile roof surface, even if it looks solid?
answer: Fragile roofing material can give way suddenly without warning regardless of its appearance, so access should use crawling boards or staging that spread the load, combined with edge protection, nets, or a harness system.

q: How often must a competent person inspect an excavation while work is ongoing?

options.A: At the start of every shift, and after any event that could affect stability
options.C: Only before the excavation is backfilled
options.D: Only if a worker reports a concern

answer: A — At the start of every shift, and after any event that could affect stability.

q: Before any excavation work begins, the site must identify the location of ______ services to avoid striking them.
answer: Underground.

q: Why must oxygen never be used to 'sweeten' the air in a confined space before entry?
answer: Adding oxygen raises its concentration well above normal, which sharply increases the risk of fire or explosion rather than making the space safer to breathe.

q: A confined space permit-to-work and rescue arrangements only need to be set up after a worker has entered and started work.
answer: False — the permit-to-work and rescue arrangements, including a lifeline, communication, a standby person, and trained rescuers, must all be in place and confirmed before anyone enters, not arranged afterward.

q: What colour are 110V reduced-voltage plugs and connectors used on UK construction sites?
answer: B — Yellow.

q: On a 110V reduced-voltage supply, the transformer's centre point is earthed so each live conductor is only around ______ volts to earth.
Why is battery-powered equipment preferred over 110V or 230V corded tools wherever practical on site?
answer: It removes the risk of electric shock from a cable or connection entirely, sitting above both 110V and 230V corded options in the hierarchy of electrical safety controls, which is why it's preferred wherever the task allows it.

q: What is the most effective way to reduce the risk from reversing vehicles on a construction site?

options.B: Use an experienced banksman for every reversing manoeuvre
options.D: Remove the need to reverse altogether, For example with a one-way system

answer: D — Remove the need to reverse altogether, For example with a one-way system.

q: A driver or crane operator must ______ immediately if they lose sight of the banksman or signaller directing them.
answer: Stop.

q: Why must the appointed person planning a lifting operation have knowledge and expertise specific to that type of lift, not just general lifting experience?
answer: Different lifts carry different risks from load geometry, surroundings, and equipment, so a plan only properly controls those risks if the person planning it understands the specific lift being carried out, not lifting in general.

q: All lifting equipment must be thoroughly examined every 12 months, with no exceptions.
answer: False — equipment used to lift people and lifting accessories such as slings must be examined every 6 months, and a written examination scheme by a competent person can set different intervals.

q: Under LOLER, how often must lifting equipment used to lift people, or lifting accessories such as slings, be thoroughly examined, where no written scheme states otherwise?
answer: C — Every 6 months.

q: Before operating any plant or vehicle, an operator must complete and sign off a ______ check at the start of each shift.
answer: Pre-use (daily).

q: Why is separating pedestrians and vehicles with distinct routes considered more effective than relying on a banksman?
answer: Segregation removes the opportunity for a pedestrian and a vehicle to be in the same space at all, so it doesn't depend on a person's attention, communication, or correct positioning the way relying on a banksman does.

q: Under the waste hierarchy, which option should always be considered first, before any other? A) Recycling
answer: C — Prevention or reduction of waste.

q: Transferring hazardous waste off site requires a hazardous waste ______ note, in addition to the standard waste transfer note.
answer: Consignment.

q: Why must rainwater collecting in a bund never be allowed to build up unchecked?
answer: It reduces the bund's spare capacity to contain a spill, and if it needs removing, it may itself count as contaminated waste requiring proper disposal.

q: There is a single fixed 'safe' date each year after which vegetation can be cleared without needing to check for nesting birds.
answer: False — the main UK breeding season runs roughly March to August but varies with weather and species, so a pre-clearance check is needed regardless of the calendar date, not a fixed safe date.

q: What capacity must a bund around a fuel storage tank provide, relative to the largest container stored within it?
Controlling dust and noise so they don't disturb neighbouring properties is an environmental ______ duty, separate from protecting workers' own health.
answer: Nuisance.

q: Why does a construction company still have a duty of care for its waste once a skip has left the site?
answer: Under the Environmental Protection Act 1990, the duty of care requires the waste producer to ensure their waste is passed only to an authorised person and properly documented, so responsibility doesn't end the moment the skip leaves site.
